paths.description: Homepage and primary headline-discovery template; tested initial consent state, desktop/mobile, preferences, performance, network, privacy, accessibility and memory.
World Cup section/listing archetype representing topical indexes and navigation into story/video content.
Representative current NewsArticle detail page, including crawler visibility, metadata and core reading flow.
Live-results interactive destination representing the scores journey and shared forms/navigation shell.
Deliberately invalid route representing HTTP/network recovery behavior.

findings.summary: A full-screen consent-or-subscribe wall obscures all editorial content on every tested entry page.
findings.evidence: Desktop and 360px screenshots show the page blurred and inert behind a modal on first load. The only prominent choices are “ACCETTA E CONTINUA” and “RIFIUTA E ABBONATI”; the latter does not provide a free rejection path.
findings.suggestedFix: Let visitors reject non-essential processing without being forced into a subscription, keep a concise non-modal notice where lawful, and use a native dialog only when blocking interaction is essential.

findings.summary: Mobile uses a scaled 1120px desktop canvas instead of a readable reflowed layout.
findings.evidence: At a 360x800 device viewport, layout reports a 1125 CSS-pixel viewport rendered at scale 0.32 because meta viewport is width=1120, initial-scale=0.70. Screenshots show tiny consent text and controls across home, article, section and live-results templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Use width=device-width, initial-scale=1; build fluid layouts with intrinsic sizing and responsive type, then verify each template at 320–412 CSS pixels.

findings.summary: The page ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark screenshot is byte-for-byte visually identical to the light capture; under emulated prefers-color-scheme: dark, computed color-scheme remains normal and body background remains rgb(253,233,235).
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and retint surfaces, text, controls and overlays with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: High-contrast preference does not change controls, and the consent UI already contains low-contrast orange text and buttons.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-contrast: more, computed colors remain unchanged. Lighthouse measures 2.83:1 for orange links/buttons and 2.29:1 for “Preferenze”, below 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase foreground/background contrast to WCAG minimums and add a prefers-contrast/forced-colors treatment that preserves borders and focus indicators.

findings.summary: Route and state changes have no View Transition integration.
findings.evidence: Rendered DOM/source feature probe found no view-transition-name, @view-transition, or related API marker on the multi-page news experience.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance same-origin article and section navigation with cross-document View Transitions, preserving an instant fallback.

findings.summary: Long pages expose no scroll-state-aware header or reading-position feedback.
findings.evidence: The homepage DOM is over 22,000px tall, while the feature probe found no scroll-state query, scroll timeline, or progress treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Add lightweight scroll-state-aware chrome or article progress where it improves orientation, with no-JS and reduced-motion fallbacks.

findings.summary: The blocking consent overlay is a custom DIV with role=dialog rather than a native dialog and has no light-dismiss path.
findings.evidence: DOM inspection reports zero <dialog> and zero popover elements; the visible 624x444 fixed overlay is a DIV role=dialog.
findings.suggestedFix: Use <dialog> for genuinely modal consent settings, label it accessibly, manage focus, and offer a clear close/reject action.

findings.summary: Initial rendering is slow and misses the good LCP threshold.
findings.evidence: Raw-CDP trace measured FCP 2.83s and LCP 4.12s; Lighthouse’s separate run measured LCP 33.5s and performance 0.48.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the true LCP resource, shorten the critical path, defer non-essential advertising/tracking, and test under representative mobile throttling.

findings.summary: Long tasks and heavy scripting block the main thread.
findings.evidence: Trace reports two long tasks, the longest 229ms, and 206ms total blocking time; Lighthouse reports 342ms TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the 229ms task, break app work into schedulable chunks, and delay advertising/analytics work until after core content is interactive.

findings.summary: The page delivers a very large, script-heavy critical path.
findings.evidence: HAR records 163 requests and 5.88MB transferred, including 2.36MB script, 2.58MB images and 682KB fonts. Parser-inserted orchestrator scripts in <head> have neither async nor defer.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer non-critical classic scripts, reduce dependency chains, subset/preload only required fonts, and prioritize only the hero image.

findings.summary: JavaScript and third-party code dominate page weight.
findings.evidence: The HAR contains 62 script requests totaling 2.36MB; Google Tag Manager alone transfers 798KB and multiple advertising/tracking bundles are among the largest resources.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit code coverage, remove duplicate/legacy bundles, and load advertising and analytics conditionally after consent and user-value content.

findings.summary: Many images and search fields lack accessible alternatives or labels.
findings.evidence: Images primitive found 43 of 100 images missing alt text. Lighthouse confirms missing alt on sponsor/footer images; DOM probe finds two search inputs without associated labels.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide meaningful alt text or alt="" for decorative images and programmatic labels for search fields; verify names and roles with axe/Lighthouse.

findings.summary: Consent links and primary controls fail WCAG contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 2.83:1 for orange-on-white links and white-on-orange buttons, and 2.29:1 for “Preferenze”, against a required 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken the orange or change text colors so normal text and controls meet at least 4.5:1 in every state.

findings.summary: Some primary interactive elements are under target size or suppress focus indication.
findings.evidence: Focus/target probe found visible controls under 44px; the Abbonamenti link computes outline: none when focused, while many other links retain the UA outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Give controls at least a 44x44 CSS-pixel activation area and use :focus-visible with a high-contrast outline on every control.

findings.summary: The mobile experience shrinks a desktop canvas rather than reflowing text and controls.
findings.evidence: A 360px device receives a 1125 CSS-pixel layout at 0.32 scale. Consent copy and controls become extremely small despite technically allowing zoom.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt device-width responsive reflow and test at 320 CSS pixels and 200% zoom without two-dimensional panning or tiny targets.

findings.summary: The page logs a resource error on load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse records a 404 for https://dimages2.gazzettaobjects.it/favicon.ico.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve the referenced favicon or remove the broken request, then verify a clean console/network load.

findings.summary: Image markup and delivery are structurally weak.
findings.evidence: Of 100 images, 80 lack explicit width/height, 35 are oversized, 41 below-fold images are not lazy-loaded and 37 use legacy formats.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio, responsive srcset/sizes, modern formats, and native lazy loading below the fold.

findings.summary: A link is not crawlable and the viewport signal is not genuinely mobile-friendly.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse flags a registration anchor with no href. The viewport is hard-coded to width=1120, producing a scaled desktop layout on mobile.
findings.suggestedFix: Give navigation anchors real href values and switch to width=device-width, initial-scale=1 with responsive templates.

findings.summary: Core transport defenses and cookie flags are missing.
findings.evidence: HTTPS is used, but headers primitive finds no CSP, HSTS or X-Content-Type-Options. Cookie audit finds 25 cookies flagged insecure and SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP, HSTS and nosniff; mark every HTTPS cookie Secure and choose Lax/Strict unless cross-site use truly requires None.

findings.summary: The initial load has an extensive tracking and third-party footprint.
findings.evidence: Tracker probe finds 30 third-party origins and five known trackers, including DoubleClick, Google Tag Manager and Facebook. HAR attributes 158 requests and 5.75MB to non-main origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize vendors and events, keep optional tags behind granular consent, batch necessary analytics, and enforce vendor budgets.

findings.summary: Visible sign-in forms rely on password fields without modern authentication or correct autofill metadata.
findings.evidence: DOM probe finds multiple text/password sign-in forms with empty autocomplete tokens and no WebAuthn/passkey marker in rendered source.
findings.suggestedFix: Add username/current-password autocomplete now and offer passkey/WebAuthn sign-in and reauthentication alongside existing methods.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are largely absent.
findings.evidence: No CSP/frame-ancestors, X-Frame-Options, HSTS, Permissions-Policy or nosniff header is present; Referrer-Policy remains no-referrer-when-downgrade.
findings.suggestedFix: Add frame-ancestors (or X-Frame-Options fallback), strict-origin-when-cross-origin Referrer-Policy, a least-privilege Permissions-Policy, HSTS, nosniff and CSP.

findings.summary: Consent choice is bundled with subscription pressure rather than offering an equivalent reject action.
findings.evidence: The modal pairs “ACCETTA E CONTINUA” with “RIFIUTA E ABBONATI”; declining profiling is framed as a paid path, while settings is a lower-emphasis orange link.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer reject-all and accept-all with equal prominence, separate consent from subscription sales, and retain easy preference reversal.

findings.summary: Search and sign-in fields omit autocomplete assistance.
findings.evidence: Rendered form probe shows search, username/text and password fields with empty autocomplete tokens.
findings.suggestedFix: Add search, username, current-password and other purpose-specific autocomplete tokens so browser assistance works reliably.

findings.summary: The subscription alternative is introduced as the only rejection path without showing price or commitment in the decision UI.
findings.evidence: The blocking wall says users can choose a paid plan but the “RIFIUTA E ABBONATI” action displays no price, term or cancellation information before the click.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a free reject path; for any subscription CTA, disclose price, billing cadence, commitment and cancellation before the user proceeds.

findings.summary: The first viewport prioritizes a long policy wall over the site’s news purpose and reading action.
findings.evidence: Across home, article, section and results screenshots, users see the policy wall instead of headlines, scores or article content.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the publication purpose and primary content visible; reduce consent copy and avoid blocking the content hierarchy.

findings.summary: The core reading flow is blocked until the visitor accepts profiling or enters a subscription path.
findings.evidence: Direct navigation to a representative article still shows only the consent-or-subscribe wall over blurred editorial content.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow the public article flow to continue after rejecting optional processing, reserving subscription gates for clearly identified paid content.

findings.summary: The content-first crawler view gives most of the first viewport to empty advertising space.
findings.evidence: No-JS crawler screenshot shows header/navigation followed by roughly 250px of blank reserved space; no headline appears in the first viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce or collapse empty ad slots before content and ensure at least one meaningful headline enters the initial viewport.

findings.summary: The component system shows no container-query adaptation and remains tied to the desktop canvas.
findings.evidence: Feature probe found no @container/container-type markers, while all three tested templates retained the 1125px CSS viewport on a 360px device.
findings.suggestedFix: Use container queries for reused cards/navigation modules and retain viewport queries only for page-level composition.

findings.summary: Images are frequently oversized, legacy-formatted and missing responsive delivery.
findings.evidence: Images probe finds 35 oversized images, 37 legacy-format images, 23 without srcset, and only one modern-format image among 100.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants and responsive srcset/sizes, and right-size author avatars and cards to rendered dimensions.

findings.summary: The page performs substantial background advertising and tracking work before content access.
findings.evidence: Initial load transfers 5.88MB in 163 requests, with 30 third-party origins and multiple tracking bundles even while the blocking consent wall is displayed.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer optional vendors until consent and idle time, remove redundant calls, and establish request/byte/CPU budgets.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts and media are disproportionate to first-viewport user value.
findings.evidence: Non-main origins account for 158 requests and 5.75MB. Scripts and images total 4.94MB while the visible state is only a consent wall.
findings.suggestedFix: Set strict third-party and media budgets, self-host essential assets, and lazy-load below-fold media only as it approaches the viewport.

findings.summary: Retained heap grows sharply after entering the site and repeatedly traversing the long feed.
findings.evidence: After GC, baseline heap was 769,639 nodes/51.1MB; after accepting the wall and ten alternating top/bottom scrolls it retained 1,417,924 nodes/83.8MB, with closures rising from 36,691 to 98,366. The consent state change is a confound, so leak attribution is medium confidence.
findings.suggestedFix: Repeat baseline/target/final snapshots in one consented session, identify retaining paths, and dispose observers, listeners, timers and ad/feed objects when no longer needed.

findings.summary: The page has a very large live heap for a news homepage.
findings.evidence: A settled baseline after GC contains 769,639 heap nodes and 51.1MB self size; the exercised state retains 83.8MB and 1.42 million nodes.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce simultaneously live cards, ad SDKs and duplicated libraries; virtualize deep feeds and enforce heap/node budgets in regression tests.

taskList.title: Replace the consent-or-subscribe wall with equal, non-blocking consent choices
Ship a true device-width responsive layout and accessible mobile reflow
Reduce critical-path, third-party, and background payload
Add CSP, HSTS, secure cookie flags, and defensive browser policies
Fix consent/UI contrast, labels, alt text, focus and target sizing
Modernize and right-size responsive image delivery
Investigate and cap retained heap growth in the feed
Honor color-scheme and improve route/scroll orientation
Add autofill tokens and passkey-capable authentication
